[ GETTING STARTED ]

Start with clarity.
One step at a time.

Debloat Android is a portable skill called android-device-care. It helps a local AI agent guide you through an Android inventory audit and produce a readable Markdown report.

Version 0.4 adds experimental third-party app disabling and restoration. Audits remain read-only. System apps, uninstall, data clearing and settings writes are blocked. Physical-device validation and backup verification are not complete.

Install the skill

To fetch the current repository on a new computer, install Git and Python, then use a fresh folder. Repository access is required while this preview remains private:

git clone https://github.com/HemantKumar822/debloat-android.git debloat-android
python debloat-android/scripts/install_skill.py --agent codex --user

On macOS/Linux use python3 if that is your Python command. Choose cursor, claude or antigravity instead of codex. If already cloned, use your existing checkout. The ZIP also includes scripts/install_skill.py, runnable from the extracted folder.

Download the portable skill ZIP and extract it. Copy its android-device-care folder into the location for your IDE below. Keep the entire folder: the skill uses the bundled Python scripts and references.

Local IDEInside your project
Codex.agents/skills/android-device-care/
Cursor.cursor/skills/android-device-care/
Claude Code.claude/skills/android-device-care/
Antigravity IDE.agents/skills/android-device-care/

Or, from a clone of the repository, use the installer. Run the dry-run first to see the destination:

python scripts/install_skill.py --agent codex --project /path/to/your/project --dry-run
python scripts/install_skill.py --agent codex --project /path/to/your/project

Replace codex with cursor, claude, or antigravity. Use --user instead of --project PATH for a personal installation. Existing installations are never overwritten. Do not install multiple copies into directories the same agent discovers.

Start with a conversation

Use android-device-care to guide me through a read-only Android audit.
Ask before reading my installed apps.

The skill should explain what it can read, guide setup, and ask for inventory consent. It runs on the computer connected to your phone. A cloud-only session cannot reach your USB device just because the skill is installed.

Prepare your computer

  1. Install Python 3.10 or newer. The audit has no third-party Python dependencies.
  2. Install Google’s Android SDK Platform Tools and make adb available on PATH.
  3. Enable Developer options and USB debugging on your Android. Connect a data-capable USB cable and approve only your trusted computer.
  4. Run the connection check from the skill folder. It does not read installed apps:
python scripts/android_care.py doctor

After agreeing to inventory collection, run:

python scripts/android_care.py audit --consent --output android-audit-report.md

For several devices, use devices to find IDs and add --serial ID. Add --save-json only if you need a machine-readable copy. When finished, turn off USB debugging or revoke the computer’s debugging access.

Try it without a phone

python scripts/android_care.py demo --output demo-android-audit.md

This creates a synthetic example. It does not connect to a device. The Markdown report opens in your editor and includes the inventory, evidence, limitations and research suggestions.

From findings to a reviewed change

For an optional third-party app, the skill can prepare a Markdown plan with its purpose, evidence, impact and a matching approval digest. You review it before anything changes. Applying repeats the device checks, saves a recovery receipt, disables one app and verifies its state.

Restoration uses the saved default/enabled state. Keep the receipt private. A lost USB connection may prevent recovery; this is not a backup or a guarantee. The workflow is experimental and has not been validated on physical devices.

Read the full plan, approval and restore instructions before opting in. The CLI requires an explicit device, experimental acknowledgement and per-document approval. No batch cleanup or system-package changes.

Privacy and evidence

The tool does not upload reports or use telemetry. Your AI provider may process information your agent reads. App names can reveal personal interests, so keep real reports private and out of public repositories.

Package names are weak research clues. They cannot establish tracking, malicious behavior, safe removal or dependency relationships. Backup status remains unverified. An inventory is not a personal-data backup.

The fixed command allowlist constrains the shipped adapter; it is not an operating-system sandbox around an unrestricted AI agent. The skill explicitly prohibits bypassing it.

What is verified?

The installation paths below were checked against official documentation on October 28, 2026. Packaging and Python tests do not constitute live validation of every IDE, Android release or manufacturer.

  • Codex documentation: project and personal .agents/skills.
  • Cursor documentation: .cursor/skills and .agents/skills. Personal skills and remote sessions have additional sync rules.
  • Claude Code documentation: .claude/skills; local and cloud sessions load skills differently.
  • Antigravity IDE documentation: project .agents/skills, personal ~/.gemini/config/skills. Antigravity CLI uses a different personal directory.

We have not yet completed a real-device matrix or live tests in all four IDEs. Unknown or failed observations stay visible; malformed or inconsistent inventory data stops the audit.

Built to be inspectable

Debloat Android is MIT licensed. The source, tests, safety architecture and roadmap live in the GitHub repository. This initial repository is private while the preview is being validated.
